# [sglang-miles] Add GPU delta decode and in-place weight updates

[Upstream PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42210) · state: open · merged: False

## Original PR description

## Motivation

@humansand

Apply canonical Miles weight deltas directly to SGLang's existing inference buffers, minimizing the time generation pauses for an update. Paired [Miles #3894](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3894); design and motivation: [GPU-accelerated Weight Teleportation](https://humansand.ai/blog/gpu-accelerated-weight-teleportation).

## Modifications

- **One update request per engine:** the Miles client supplies the admitted participants, session, publication and version information. SGLang prepares in the background, pauses and fences readers, applies on every original rank, then resumes that engine. Independent engines can resume separately; Miles advances its publication baseline after all engines finish. Preparation failure leaves old-version serving available. Uncertain XOR application is never retried or replayed.
- **Preparation outside the pause:** authenticate the manifest; read and optionally hash payload files into shared tmpfs; unwrap outer Zstd into reusable, rank-local HOST_NUMA arenas; prepare small GPU metadata, raw-value targets and derived calibration. Bulk host copies release the GIL. Preparation does not modify live weights or KV storage, pause generation, or synchronize the generation stream. Concurrent-serving throughput impact remains unmeasured.
- **Fixed decode/apply pipeline:** one hardware-DE stream and one Triton apply stream alternate exactly two decoded HBM slots. Slot reuse waits for the preceding apply. Native size/status checks gate XOR and derived-weight updates. Slots are allocated only after the reader fence and released before resume; failures drain both streams before releasing their storage. There is no encoded HBM ring or configurable pipeline depth.
- **Layout and kernel contract:** admission describes native packed weights as affine byte views; padding is excluded and aliases receive one XOR. Fresh frame metadata accounts for omitted unchanged ranges. Three fixed Triton access families cover packed, word-affine and general byte layouts; only families with work launch. Geometry and launch bindings are cached, with no workload-dependent compilation keys, online autotuning or update-time weight permutation.
- **Native decoding:** call the 64-bit nvCOMP 6 C API directly, using caller-owned output, status and workspace allocations. DE capability, frame limits, alignment and capacity are checked explicitly; no software-decompression fallback. Temporary-workspace sizes are cached by batch geometry and stream. Validated package: `nvidia-libnvcomp-cu13==6.0.0.12` (`libnvcomp.so.6`).
- **Ownership and observability:** HTTP/IPC control, host storage, layout admission and DE/apply code remain under `srt/weight_sync/gpu_delta/`; ordinary loading and disk-update paths are reused or left unchanged. Rank/engine timing, byte and buffer metrics remain available to Miles/W&B. `SGLANG_ENABLE_NVTX_OPERATIONS=1` adds detailed CPU and enqueue ranges; the benchmark controls capture.

### API and use

These HTTP POST endpoints are an internal interface to Miles:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/get_gpu_delta_info` | Admit the receiver and return its canonical plan, original participants and version. |
| `/update_weights_from_gpu_delta` | Prepare, apply and resume one publication; return APPLIED/RESUMED receipts and metrics. |
| `/get_gpu_delta_status` | Inspect an identified session without repeating its update. |
| `/clear_gpu_delta_state` | Release retained delta resources while preserving weights and committed version. |

`validate_payload_hash=True` controls payload SHA256 verification. Disabling it skips payload hashes only; manifest authentication, exact file extent/identity and native decoding checks remain. `release_state=True` combines a successful update with resource cleanup; default `False` retains caches for the next update. Cleanup is outside activation timings. Existing caller-owned pauses are preserved.

Ordinary updates use consecutive transport versions. A fresh version-0 engine can recover from its matching immutable HF checkpoint through the same API. Miles exclusively owns updates, pause/resume and topology for the stream; other writers, rollback and automatic recovery from uncertain application are outside this contract. See the [receiver guide](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/9747f67b11f64ad17d5a9e5a26cbac02c80388f9/test/registered/unit/gpu_delta_weight_sync/README.md) for lifecycle, payload and configuration details.

### Compatibility

Blackwell hardware DE and CUDA 13; Snappy–Zstd, LZ4–Zstd and plain LZ4, with frames up to 4 MiB subject to the device's compressed/decompressed limits. Current model mappings cover the DeepSeek MLA/DSA family and GLM's shared implementation. Bundled MTP layers remain static; shared embedding/head buffers follow the target.

| Native weight format | FlashInfer TRTLLM / routed | CuTe DSL | MegaMoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | Yes | — | — |
| FP8 128×128, UE8M0 scales | Yes | — | — |
| MXFP8 | Yes | — | Yes |
| MXFP4 × MXFP8 activation | Yes | — | Yes |
| NVFP4 | W4A4 | W4A4 / W4A16 | W4A4 / W4A16 |

These are admitted layouts for existing inference backends, not full-serving qualification of every combination. No weight requantization or conversion fallback is supported. Compact UE8M0 scales expand losslessly for existing FP32 API images; arbitrary FP32 scales are rejected. CuTe wrappers and derived buffers must already exist. TRTLLM NVFP4 with clamped activation requires tied gate/up global scales; an update requiring block-scale requantization is rejected before mutation.

Routed experts require fixed topology, expert TP=1 and an unsharded canonical checkpoint; no EPLB, redundant experts or elastic joins. The Python server requires global control broadcast, attention TP/CP/DCP=1 and PP=1; LoRA, disaggregated serving, shared IPC weights and unsupported derived-weight caches are excluded. Delta application introduces no distributed data collectives.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Environment and methodology

- **Hardware/image:** 8 × NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, 256 logical CPUs; `radixark/miles:dev-202611021910`, amd64 digest `sha256:5f4f74c8f5e89d7af90595f7ab8717588fed86b4506ad5fc4b0d9865cbcb903a`.
- **Runtime:** Python 3.12.16, Torch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Transformer Engine 2.17.0+miles, Ray 2.58.1, pytest 9.2.0, NVIDIA driver 595.91.07. Package comparison: `nvidia-libnvcomp-cu13==5.3.0.16` versus `6.0.0.12`; all other installed distributions were unchanged.
- **Source attribution:** the comparison includes the required C-ABI adaptation and library upgrade together. It does not isolate library-only causality. The current Miles head changes only the five-layer CI test relative to the measured Miles revision; production and benchmark code are identical.

The five-layer CI test includes warm gates of **prepare <6 s, scheduler pause <0.3 s and measured encoding stages <6 s**, with cold/empty work excluded and rewarming after receiver replacement. These bounds are informed by the full-model proxy; the five-layer E2E and its workload-specific calibration have **not been run**. Its helper logic has local validation only. Separate eval-engine E2E is excluded because the eight-GPU training/rollout workload cannot host another eval engine.

### Receiver benchmark

- **Workload:** full GLM-5.2 NVFP4 W4A16; Snappy–Zstd, 1 MiB frames, three cumulative versions, mutation ratio 0.002 and seed 20261001. Two TP4/attention-DP4/EP4 engines use eight GPUs. Fixed double buffering, one model layer per batch, 32 CPU workers, CuTe DSL MoE, FP8 KV, page size 64, MRR128, EAGLE with 3 steps/4 draft tokens, CUDA graphs batch 1/max 1, FlashInfer autotuning off and Python TreeCore.
- **Method:** reuse the same authenticated SHA-on publications and prepared snapshots. Hash OFF changes only receiver `validate_payload_hash`; sender checksums and manifest/fixture admission remain enabled. Fresh processes run serially, with no input encoding, Nsight capture or final-target oracle in these receiver runs.
- **Timing:** preparation is rank host wall; pause is scheduler pause through successful resume; apply is paused worker host wall; coordinator is the enclosing Miles await. Values below are maxima across eight ranks, except the single enclosing coordinator duration in the raw aggregates. Spans overlap and must not be added. v1 is first use in a fresh process, not a cleared host/compiler cache; v2/v3 are distinct cumulative warm updates, not statistical repetitions.
- **Coverage:** each of four runs completed 24 APPLIED/24 RESUMED records, generation on all eight routes for every version, and eight clears. All hash-OFF rank records reported zero payload-SHA bytes, files and worker time.

| Hash | Update | Prepare max s: 5.3 → 6 | Change | Pause max ms: 5.3 → 6 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| on | v1 cold | 20.172168 → 10.245155 | -49.211% | 356.337890 → 3806.713046 | +968.287% |
| on | v2 warm | 4.405531 → 4.158098 | -5.616% | 228.558447 → 244.084626 | +6.793% |
| on | v3 warm | 3.675636 → 3.905894 | +6.264% | 235.602636 → 232.738178 | -1.216% |
| off | v1 cold | 9.255014 → 10.343810 | +11.764% | 358.218978 → 3730.783078 | +941.481% |
| off | v2 warm | 3.737366 → 3.828195 | +2.430% | 236.131522 → 228.003211 | -3.442% |
| off | v3 warm | 3.538192 → 3.386381 | -4.291% | 230.434475 → 232.892878 | +1.067% |

The nvCOMP 6 warm pause maxima are **228.003–244.085 ms**; warm preparation is **3.386–4.158 s**. Relative to nvCOMP 5.3, individual warm preparation changes range from −5.616% to +6.264%, and pause changes from −3.442% to +6.793%. These observations do not establish statistical performance equivalence.

**Cold pause regressed:** 0.356338 → 3.806713 s with hashing on and 0.358219 → 3.730783 s with hashing off. Existing timers do not identify the cause; this is not a blanket no-regression result.

### Producer compression benchmark

- **Workload:** the same preserved prepared snapshots, fresh Snappy–Zstd/1 MiB encoding, payload SHA on, eight whole-layer HF owners and three versions. No input generation, receiver/model-engine load, final oracle or Nsight capture. READY metadata, settings, sizes and plan identity are checked; no new full tensor-byte rehash is claimed.
- **Encoding wall:** for each owner, `encode_stage_wall_s = batch_wall_s + finalization_wall_s`; report the maximum of those owner totals. It includes H2D, XOR, compression, metadata, packing and final D2H. Separately measured input reads, publication writes and parent sealing are excluded.
- **Compression timing:** CUDA events bracket each actual nvCOMP `CompressAsync` call on its passed stream/device; host API wall is measured separately. Events are resolved after the existing final fence. Sum sequential calls within each owner, then take maxima. Stream spans include native work and possible host-submission gaps; they are not pure kernel durations. Both arms include the same instrumentation. Overlapping spans and independent maxima are not additive.

| Update | Encoding-stage max s: 5.3 → 6 | Change | nvCOMP stream-span max ms: 5.3 → 6 | Change | nvCOMP host-API max ms: 5.3 → 6 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 cold | 9.310264 → 6.312708 | -32.196% | 1929.985315 → 1930.480160 | +0.026% | 6.189892 → 5.960200 | -3.711% |
| v2 warm | 5.065410 → 5.309824 | +4.825% | 1928.730721 → 1928.582439 | -0.008% | 4.069090 → 3.848642 | -5.418% |
| v3 warm | 5.023624 → 5.139641 | +2.309% | 1928.916740 → 1929.279484 | +0.019% | 4.718624 → 5.420088 | +14.866% |

No compression-throughput improvement was observed: warm nvCOMP stream spans changed by −0.008%/+0.019%, while enclosing encoding wall increased by +4.825%/+2.309%. All three versions have identical payload-size accounting across the two arms; this does not assert encoded-byte identity.

Use the exact source/library pair and image above. The retained full-model checkpoint and prepared snapshots are external inputs. Generating replacements changes the experiment. <details>
<summary>Producer-only timing recipe and command</summary>

The command requires project-only `producer_only.py`, SHA256 `65d94ca61b9d87977fc86b0cf63dd6b3b781cd7820101ffd539a9764b4bed26f`, kept separate from the receiver overlay. Each spawned owner imports the committed benchmark and wraps `NvcompCompressor.__init__` to instrument `_compress` as follows.

```python
# Inside each compressor's init wrapper, retain native = self._compress.
def compress(*args):
    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(self.device)
    assert len(args) == 11 and stream.cuda_stream == args[-1]
    start, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
    start.record(stream)
    t = time.monotonic()
    status = native(*args)
    host_api_s = time.monotonic() - t
    end.record(stream)
    calls.append((self.codec, args, self.device.index, start, end, host_api_s))
    return status
# After original _encode_version returns, existing finish_device fencing has
# completed these events. Resolve start.elapsed_time(end)/1000, retain actual
# stream args[-1]/device and per-call host wall, then clear calls. No new fence.
```

Call `_load_prepared_inputs` then `_fixture` with `versions=3, seed=20261001, ratio=0.002, frame_bytes=1048576, sender_gpus=8`, inventory `prepared_inputs/inventory/inventory.json`, target `prepared_inputs/target-checkpoint`, arm `snappy-zstd-hash-on`, and loaded mutation rate. Record owner/per-call measurements; do not load receiver engines or run the final oracle.

```bash
# Use S, P and the shared environment above; disable NVTX.
R=/path/to/producer-only-helper-directory
O=/path/to/fresh/compression-operation
mkdir "$O"
"$P" - "$S" "$O" <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
s, o = (Path(x).resolve() for x in sys.argv[1:])
q = {
    "source": str(s), "operation": str(o),
    "benchmark_source_sha256": hashlib.sha256((s / "miles/tests/manual/gpu_delta/bench_gpu_delta.py").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
    "model": "/data/models/ziangli_glm52/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-W4A16",
    "inputs": {"prepared_inputs": "/data/ziangli/gpu-delta-20261001/benchmark121-run001/inputs001",
               "input_ready_sha256": "8a9a2be454f1a872256ef431b2652dae7517ff732ea3f0ce0d0236f133b883e2"},
}
with (o / "REQUEST.json").open("x") as f:
    json.dump(q, f, indent=2)
PY
export PYTHONPATH="$S/miles/tests/manual/gpu_delta:$S/sglang/python:$S/miles"
export GPU_DELTA_CODEC=snappy-zstd GPU_DELTA_SKIP_PAYLOAD_HASH=0
"$P" -B "$R/producer_only.py" --request "$O/REQUEST.json"
```

The producer-only helper is external to these PRs. The snippet specifies its timing boundary; the command requires that exact helper and the retained prepared inputs.

</details>

**Validation limits:** no full-model final-weight oracle, full RL run, concurrent rollout-throughput study or complete backend/format E2E matrix is claimed by these measurements. Import/startup latency is excluded from update timings. The performance proxy covers Snappy–Zstd/1 MiB with receiver hashing on/off; native roundtrip tests also cover LZ4 and Zstd.
